name: PT Indomobil Sukses Internasional Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indomobil: out of the index, beneath what the parts are worth
frontmatter.summary: FTSE Russell deletes Indomobil on 21 December and MSCI decides on Standalone status by 30 June. Neither sets value: the parts are worth Rp887 a share against a price of Rp695, with half the appraisal reserve now admitted and the listed subsidiary at its house fundamental. The regime lens slows the climb to Rp803: ADD.
thesis: On its parts the group is worth Rp887 a share against a price of Rp695: the listed Indomobil Multi Jasa stake at its house fundamental, the rest at pre-appraisal book plus half the land and property reserve, after a wide holdco discount and the liquidity ladder [S5][S3].

The appraisal reserve is the swing factor and it is now half in the base: valuing it at cost leaves the parts below the price, valuing it at the appraised mark well above it, so the ruling matters more than any car-market forecast [S3][S5].

The twelve-month call is the regime, not the assets: at 0.88 times fundamental value the shares are below what the parts are worth, and the engine keeps only part of that gap over a year, closing 25% of it in the base case [S0][S16].

The flow backdrop is negative and dated: HSC-listed, out of the IHSG since 13 November, deleted from the FTSE Russell global indices at the open on 21 December, with a free float of 7.3% against the exchange's fifteen per cent floor and an MSCI Standalone decision due by 30 June 2027 [S16][S17][S18][S20].

Operating cash flow has broken: an outflow in the nine months to September 2026, financial liabilities due within a year an order of magnitude above cash, and an interest bill that consumes almost all of operating income [S3][S5].

Earnings quality: FY2025 profit carries a one-off bargain-purchase gain and the group pays tax at the rate the LK shows, not the statutory rate, so parent earnings are near zero before any of that [S5][S3].

catalysts.event: FTSE Russell deletes the HSC-category names, Indomobil among them, from its global indices at the open; the last index bid for the shares goes with it [S16].
Full-year Gaikindo wholesales and the group December volume report; the market is within two average months of the association target, so the test is share and margin, not market size [S6][S11][S12].

FY2026 audited accounts — refinancing of the short-term book, any going-concern emphasis, the first full year of the INA consolidation — and the FTSE March review at which the postponed reclassification could return [S3][S9][S16].

MSCI closes the consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status and decides by the end of June; retention in the emerging-market index is the one dated regime catalyst that works the other way [S20].
Annual general meeting and the dividend decision; the parent payout is the only cash return the minority controls [S8].

blocks.text: **What changed, and what did not.** Our last published call was a sell, at a target below the price. The rating is now ADD with a target of Rp803, 15.6% from Rp695. Two things changed, and neither is the 21 December FTSE deletion: the 11 November high-shareholding-concentration listing put the name into the regime lens, which asks how much of the gap between price and value closes inside twelve months rather than whether it closes at all; and this revision admits half of the land and property appraisal reserve, which the previous edition zeroed with a reason that leaned on the share price; the valuation section corrects that [S19][S16].

**Why ADD, not a sell and not a buy.** The parts are worth Rp887 a share against Rp695, so the shares trade at 0.88 times what the assets justify — a discount, not a premium [S5][S3]. The lens does not close a discount instantly: the base regime case closes 25% of the logarithmic gap, the regime bear -20% in the other direction, the regime bull 65%, weighted 50% base, 25% bear and 25% bull, which is the target [S0][S16]. The 13 November close of 695.0 predates the 14 November announcement, so it says nothing about how the market took the deletion; and it sits near the 675.0 low and far below the 1,385.0 high, which is where a stock that has already lost its index demand trades — we do not read it as support [S0][S16].

The operating story is still weak. Nine-month revenue grew on a market that grew faster, yet gross margin fell and parent profit collapsed, because discounting and imported-unit costs consumed the gain; finance charges of 2,585.5 against operating income of 2,820.5 leave cover near one time, and operating cash flow was an outflow with liabilities due within a year at IDR36,146.9bn against cash of IDR3,158.6bn [S3][S5].

The parts are the 92.0% IMJS stake at its house fundamental and the non-IMJ businesses at book plus half the appraisal reserve, less a holdco discount at the wide end of the house band [S5][S3][S8]. The ladder has three steps and the first is the largest: Rp1,003 a share after the holdco discount, Rp1,109 after the twelve-month roll and the business-scenario weights, Rp887 after the liquidity ladder [S0][S3]. The price sits below all three, which is why the fundamental case is no longer a sell; the target falls short of fundamental value because the lens expects only part of the gap to close. What would change the view is realisation of the withheld half of the reserve, a float fix that restores index eligibility, or an MSCI decision to keep Indonesia in the emerging-market index [S3][S8][S20].

Indomobil is a holding company whose revenue comes from vehicle distribution and after-sales, consumer financing and leasing, rental and logistics, and a residual group of industrial, property and service businesses. The automotive segment earns most of the revenue but, after allocation of finance income and charges, lost IDR-4,075.9bn in FY2025 while the smaller segments carried consolidated profit: distribution loses money at the net level before the parent interest bill [S5].

The "Others" segment earned IDR1,892.8bn in FY2025 and holds the industrial and property assets, but part of that result is non-recurring bargain-purchase gains on the INA, RMM and ISJ acquisitions [S5]. We therefore do not capitalise its earnings; we carry its assets at book before the appraisal marks [S3][S5]. The distribution arm sells Japanese and European franchises through a partly owned dealer network; the finance arm lends to buyers; the rental arm leases a fleet [S5][S10].

The group is also a battery-electric participant: it owns a majority of Aion Indomobil Distribution Indonesia, all of Indomobil Zeeda Energi and 99.9% of INA (formerly NMI), all inside the consolidated segments and therefore inside the book we value [S5].

Indomobil is one of the oldest automotive groups in Indonesia, built from a trading house into a distributor, assembler and financier. Distribution earns a thin gross margin on a large revenue base and needs working capital; the finance arm earns a spread on a book funded with borrowings; the holding company above both services the debt that funded the build-out, so consolidated profit is more sensitive to the funding mix than to the number of cars sold.

Control is concentrated and the free float is 7.3%, below the minimum public shareholding the exchange applies: that floor rose from seven and a half per cent to fifteen per cent with effect from March 2026, so the stock fails the test on either rule [S0][S15]. No special-monitoring-board status or special notation letter appears in the 2024 annual report or the September interim filing [S10][S3]. The governance section sets out the register, the HSC status and the index position.

The Indonesian car market is a volume market with policy-driven costs. Wholesales reached 679,020 units in nine months and 760,476 in ten, so October ran at 81,482, 10.0% above October 2025's 74,051 [S6][S11][S13]. The ten-month rate is 19.7% on the 635,456-unit base, below the nine-month 21.0%; the higher figure one outlet prints divides the ten-month total by the nine-month base [S11][S14][S6]. The association target needs less than the current run rate over two months, so the constraint has moved to margin [S6]. Battery-electric vehicles took 15.9% of the market in the first half [S7].

For an incumbent the transition is a margin problem before a volume problem. The portfolio is weighted toward Japanese combustion models that carry the workshop annuity; a battery-electric fleet needs less servicing and is sold by competitors without the legacy cost base [S7][S10]. The group has added agency agreements and the INA assembly acquisition rather than build its own brand [S9][S5]. Its scale and workshop footprint are real, but the moat is contractual, not structural: Chinese manufacturers appoint new distributors and build their own networks, so share is lost rather than recirculated [S6][S7][S9].
Suzuki, a volume brand the group assembles and distributes, sold 59,328 units in ten months for a 7.8% share, while BYD alone sold 50,366 [S12][S5].

The Indonesian car market is a cyclical volume market driven by household credit, the rupiah and the policy treatment of luxury goods. Distributors earn a gross margin on the vehicle, a second margin on financing arranged through a captive or partner finance company, and a third, higher-margin annuity on parts and labour over the life of the car. That third leg is why the dealer network has value beyond the showroom, and it is the leg a battery-electric fleet erodes.
Final income tax is levied on turnover, a fixed cost per unit irrespective of profitability, and luxury-goods tax and down-payment rules move demand between quarters [S5][S6].

Revenue compounded at a mid-single-digit rate to FY2025 and grew faster in the nine months to September 2026: 30,505.5 for the prior full year against IDR22,720.8bn for the comparable nine months [S5][S3]. It is not translating into profit — gross margin fell, operating income was below the prior-year comparable and parent profit was IDR15.2bn [S3].

The fourth quarter needs no heroics. We take nine-month revenue of IDR27,492.6bn, add a fourth quarter grown at October's 10.0% market rate rather than the nine-month pace, and get FY2026E revenue of 36,057.5, 18.2% on FY2025A [S3][S13]. That assumes no share gain and no price recovery; faster growth would need a fourth quarter accelerating against a decelerating market [S6][S11].

Costs are dominated by two items the equity holder cannot influence: finance charges of 2,585.5 set by the debt stock and rate, and depreciation of 1,351.4 set by the asset base; together they exceed operating income [S5]. We restate depreciation to the audited total, roughly three times the pack figure, and dividends paid to the parent amount, because the pack includes the distribution to non-controlling interests [S5][S8].

Tax is the prior draft's error. Nine-month income tax was IDR266.8bn on pre-tax profit of IDR330.5bn, and it is not a one-off: current tax alone was IDR303.7bn with IDR177.0bn of permanent differences, and the charge barely moved from the prior year although pre-tax profit halved [S3]. The engine taxes levered pre-tax profit, so FY2026E carries that rate, fading to statutory only as the loss-making units return to profit, and FY2026E parent profit is 56.1 [S3][S5]. The convention has to be stated beside it: the engine charges interest at the modelled rate on the opening balance, 2,566.6, whereas nine months already charged IDR2,033.8bn on gross borrowings that rose during the year [S3]. Annualised, the actual sits above the modelled line, so the run rate is lower than the forecast and the nine-month actual of IDR15.2bn is the honest anchor; nothing in the target depends on it [S3][S5]. On the audited year the same arithmetic gave tax of 375.8 on pre-tax profit of 608.2 [S5].

Cash generation is the central operating problem: capex of 2,890.2 exceeded operating cash flow of IDR2,040.2bn in the audited year, and the nine months produced an operating outflow of IDR-4,967.1bn as the finance book and inventory absorbed cash [S5][S3]. Our forecast carries capex converging toward depreciation plus growth, working capital at the observed level to revenue, and net new borrowing that funds the gap [S3][S5]. Free cash flow to the firm is IDR-4,251.0bn in FY2026E and turns positive only in the final years [S5].

Debt is short and large: liabilities due within a year are an order of magnitude above cash, with little committed undrawn capacity disclosed [S3]. The finance subsidiaries bond-fund the loan book, but parent lines roll quarterly, so a funding-market closure transmits into a liquidity event; net debt at 30 September already exceeded the model's FY2026E line on the engine's cash balances, which the valuation does not use [S3][S5].

Earnings quality is tested on the right basis for a finance book. The Sloan ratio is meaningless here; the test is provisioning against write-offs, receivables written off once overdue more than six months [S5]. The appraisal reserve in equity is IDR6,847.1bn, and IDR3,240.0bn of investment-property fair value sits inside it, so book value is a mark rather than a cost [S5][S3].

We value the group on its parts: a claim on a listed subsidiary plus operating and property assets [S5][S3]. The cost of equity is 11.9%, from the 7.4% risk-free rate the house deck takes from the ten-year government yield [S21], a 4.2% mature-market premium, a 2.5% country premium and a 2.30 levered beta built from the 0.90 asset beta at the capped 2.00 consolidated gearing [S0]. That cap is the problem: it levers the asset beta to the rate of a distressed stub, while the SOTP is already an equity value net of every subsidiary's debt, holdco net debt is nil, and the consolidated gearing is priced once through the holdco discount. The -9.3% company adjustment removes the double count and lands the cost of equity at 11.9%, inside the house eleven-to-thirteen-per-cent band [S3]. The WACC printed beside it, 8.9%, is not a discount rate here: no cash flow is discounted, because the SOTP is a net asset value rolled twelve months at the cost of equity.

The first block is the 92.0% stake in PT Indomobil Multi Jasa, marked at the subsidiary's own house fundamental, not at its share price [S0]. IMJS is itself a concentrated-ownership name — 94.9% in the exchange's HSC figure, out of the IHSG since 13 November, with only the stake we do not own as float — so its price carries the same regime discount and marking it at market would import a regime variable into the parent's fundamental value [S19][S5]. A covered sibling is marked pre-lens and the parent's lens is applied once afterwards; the difference is under a tenth of the parent's value, but it is disclosed rather than left as an accident of the tape.

The second block is the non-IMJ businesses at pre-appraisal book equity attributable to Indomobil, net of the IMJ stake and non-controlling interests, plus half of the appraisal reserve [S3]. The reserve is the whole mark above cost inside other equity at 30 September 2026: land revaluation of IDR3,688.6bn plus IDR3,240.0bn of investment properties recognised at fair value, IDR6,847.1bn at the prior year-end [S3][S5]. It is the single largest judgement in the target. Half is admitted because valuing land and income-producing property at cost puts assets at a figure no independent appraisal supports; half is withheld because no sale, sale-and-leaseback or disposal process is disclosed, a disposal at the mark would attract tax on the gain and a block-size discount on assets of this scale, and no transaction has tested the mark [S5][S3]. The split is half because that is the midpoint of the two defensible marks, and it is set from the assets, not from the share price.

The block is not an industrial cushion. Investments in shares are IDR4,300.4bn — IDR2,580.6bn of associates at equity-method carrying value and IDR1,719.7bn of unquoted shares at fair value — beside IDR3,220.2bn of related-party receivables [S3]. Those two lines alone exceed the block, so the operating businesses and the parent's corporate debt net to a negative book inside it; the franchise is floored at zero rather than valued at a loss, which is the honest reading of a distributor whose segment lost IDR-4,075.9bn at the net level in FY2025 [S5][S3]. Revenue is not an asset for a loss-making distributor; a margin recovery is what would create value there, and the FY2026 audited accounts will show it or not [S3]. The associates earned IDR143.1bn in nine months with no impairment charged, so carrying value has no independent test either [S3][S5].

We apply a holdco discount of 40%, at the wide end of the house band, and the liquidity ladder takes a further 20% because the stock trades below the minimum turnover threshold [S8][S3]. Concentrated control, a thin float, related-party purchases at a fifth of cost of revenue, a large claim on affiliates and an equity base half of which is appraisal justify the wide end [S8][S3][S5]. Price to book was 0.2x, and the house base rate for a discount of this kind narrowing within three years is about one case in three, from the internal base-rate file rather than from the market [S3][S5].

So the ladder is: Rp1,003 a share after the holdco discount, Rp1,109 after the twelve-month roll at 11.9% and the business-scenario weights (45% base, 30% bear, 25% bull), Rp887 after the liquidity ladder [S0][S3]. The discount, not the ladder or the roll, is the large step — that ordering tells the reader which judgement to test.

The sensitivity that matters is the discount, not the discount rate: the grid moves the value by roughly one-sixth either side for a ten-point change in the holdco discount, double the effect of the same change in the cost of equity.

**The appraisal range, run through the target.** Because the reserve is the largest judgement, we ran both ends through the whole model, not a single sensitivity cell. Admitting none of it, the previous edition's position, puts the parts below the price and the call at a hold with a negative expected return; admitting all of it puts the target a quarter above the price and the call at a buy; the base admits half and is an ADD [S3][S5]. The call is therefore not an artefact of the midpoint, and it would take a move to one extreme of the evidence to make it a sell.

The consolidated cash flow is a cross-check, not a weighted method: free cash flow to the firm is negative through the middle of the forecast, so the enterprise value floors at zero [S5][S3]. The earnings multiple is unavailable because FY2025 profit is inflated by the "Others" segment result and the bargain-purchase gains [S3][S5]. What the price implies is in 0.6 of the valuation grid.

**The konglo lens.** Indomobil is on the HSC list with 95.5% of the shares in the concentrated holdings the exchange publishes against a float of 7.3%, so a few per cent of the register sets the price [S19][S0]. The engine values the parts first — 792.4 in today's money and Rp887 in twelve months — and measures the price against the first: Rp695 over 792.4 is 0.88, a discount, a log gap of -0.13 [S0][S16]. In a discount the regime flags slow the climb rather than speed it: HSC membership and the 21 December deletion remove the marginal buyer while the controller does not sell, so the base case closes 25% of the gap for Rp804, the regime bear closes -20% for Rp758, and the regime bull closes 65% for Rp847, weighted 50%/25%/25% to Rp803 [S0][S16][S20]. HSC membership adds 5% to the closing share; the free-float deadline falls outside the window and no enforcement is recorded [S16][S15].

The downside is a governance and funding discount, not demand. If the finance book stops growing and defaults rise, the group loses the profit centre carrying the consolidated result while the interest bill on the short book is unchanged [S3][S5]. Because liabilities due within a year dwarf cash, a refusal by banks to roll the lines would force asset sales at the worst point, and the appraisal reserve is not cash [S3][S5]. The bear widens the discount rather than revaluing the block, and the zero-admission end of the reserve range is run separately in the valuation section; that is why the bear stays at 30% even though the demand data are positive — it is a funding and governance case, and volume at 10.0% leaves that channel untouched [S13][S14]. Base stays at 45% and bull at 25%.

A discounted equity raise has to be run both ways, because it is simultaneously the bear's dilution and the one documented route out of the regime. As a downside: at a fraction of book, with control at 49.5% and a float of 7.3%, the cheapest recapitalisation is a discounted placement or rights issue, which transfers value to the subscriber, and we carry it in the bear as a wider discount because the size is undisclosed [S8][S3]. As an upside: a placement of new shares to the public is exactly what closes the 7.7% percentage-point gap to the 15.0% floor; issuing roughly a tenth of the existing share count at a discount would take the float over the floor, cost existing holders a few per cent of net asset value a share, and restore eligibility for the indices the shares have just left [S15][S17]. We give the float-fixing placement about a one-in-four chance inside the window — it needs the controller's consent, which the Salim group has never signalled, and the small-cap deadline runs to 2029, so there is no compulsion before then [S15][S8]. It is the same transaction the bear runs as dilution; we will not carry it as a downside only.

**The flows are sized, not asserted.** The shares left the IHSG calculation on 13 November and leave the FTSE global indices at the open on 21 December [S17][S16]. Average daily turnover is IDR250,423,269.8bn against a market capitalisation of IDR2,776,032,272,105.0bn and a float of 7.3% [S0], so the entire free float is worth several years of average daily turnover: a passive holder exiting even a fraction of it cannot be absorbed without a price concession. That is the mechanical reason the base case leaves 25% of the gap unclosed and the bear closes -20% the other way [S0][S16]. The tracker holding is not disclosed; the float arithmetic bounds it from above, and the bound already binds.

**The MSCI decision is the remaining regime catalyst.** MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 on moving Indonesia to Standalone status, with feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by end-June, and the freeze on index increases for Indonesian securities remains until further notice [S20]. That date is inside our window and it is the one event that could work the other way: an adverse decision removes the remaining index demand permanently and pushes the closure share from the base 25% toward the regime bear's -20%, near Rp758, while retention in the emerging-market index is the dated catalyst behind the regime bull's 65% and Rp847 [S20][S16]. We date both tails rather than forecast the outcome.

**Two scenario sets, not one.** The business scenarios above are about the assets; the regime scenarios are about the price of a concentrated-ownership micro cap and are independent of them [S16][S0]. In the regime bear the deletion, the HSC exclusion and an adverse MSCI outcome close -20% of the log gap over twelve months (Rp758); in the regime base 25% (Rp804); in the regime bull a float fix or an MSCI retention closes 65% (Rp847). The weights are 50% base, 25% bear and 25% bull, taken from the house konglo deck [S16][S20]. The mirror is exact in the business set, where the bull applies the same discount channel in the opposite amount: the probability-weighted business value is Rp1,109, the liquidity ladder takes it to Rp887, and the lens sets the twelve-month target at Rp803 [S0][S8]. We also tested the rating against the weights: doubling the bear weight and halving the base still leaves the target above the price, because the discount to value is wide enough to absorb it, so the call does not rest on a single weight [S0][S16].

Other risks are structural. The rupiah matters through imported-unit costs and foreign-currency debt, and derivative liabilities have moved against the group [S3]. Related-party purchases at a fifth of cost of revenue make transfer pricing a live risk, and a single point on the short-term rate changes the interest bill by more than parent profit [S3][S5].

Signposts that would change our view: the MSCI decision on 30 June 2027; a term extension beyond a year; a disposal or sale-and-leaseback of industrial or property assets at appraised value, which would realise the withheld half of the reserve; a dividend upstream from the listed subsidiary; a float-fixing placement, which we would read as dilutive per share but positive for the regime; and a sustained gross-margin recovery with positive operating cash flow [S3][S5][S8][S20].

The controller is the Salim group. Gallant Venture, its Singapore-listed holding company whose control sits with Anthoni Salim, holds 49.5% of Indomobil; PT Tritunggal Intipermata, PT Trimegah Sekuritas Indonesia and PT Sejahtera Raya Perkasa hold most of the rest, and the annual report's public bucket — holders below five per cent — is 12.1% while the exchange's free-float figure is 7.3% [S10][S0]. The register counts strategic holders as public, the exchange does not: on the exchange's number the shares are on the HSC list with 95.5% of the stock in the concentrated holdings it publishes [S19]. Indomobil is the group's Indonesian distribution, assembly and multi-finance vehicle, with the multi-finance arm separately listed and 92.0% owned [S5].

The same regime runs one level down, and it matters for how the largest block is valued. IMJS is on the HSC list at 94.9%, so its only float is the 92.0% stake IMAS does not own; it left the IHSG calculation on the same day as its parent [S19][S17]. That is precisely why the valuation section marks the stake at the subsidiary's house fundamental and not at its market price: a market with an eight-per-cent float and no index bid does not set an asset value, it sets a regime price, and carrying that price into the parent's fundamental value would double-count one regime discount into the other [S19][S5][S0]. The difference is under a tenth of the parent's value today, but the direction is structural and we would rather label it than be right by accident.

The index and float position binds. HSC status took the shares out of the IHSG calculation on 13 November and out of the LQ45, the IDX30 and the IDX80, and FTSE Russell deletes them from its global indices at the open on 21 December [S17][S18][S16]. The free float is 7.3% against the exchange's fifteen per cent floor, and the small-cap timetable runs to 2029, so nothing forces a fix inside our window [S15][S0]. No pledge of the controlling stake is disclosed in the annual report or the interim filing, and we find no enforcement action [S10][S3].

Related-party dealings are large and recurring: purchases from related parties were IDR4,902.6bn in nine months, about a fifth of cost of revenue, and other receivables from related parties stood at IDR3,220.2bn, a claim on affiliates and the clearest channel through which value can leave the group [S3]. The FY2025 accounts were audited without modification, but the land revaluation of IDR3,688.6bn and the investment-property fair value of IDR3,240.0bn sit inside equity, so book value is a mark [S5][S3]. Minority dividends of a large multiple of the parent dividend show where the cash goes [S5][S8].

ESG exposures are electrification, workshop emissions and consumer-finance lending into an indebted household sector [S7][S3]. Governance dominates: a thin float, a controller with related interests, large related-party flows and a revaluation-heavy equity base [S8].

The nearest dated catalyst is the regime one: FTSE Russell deletes the shares from its global indices at the open on 21 December 2026, after which there is no index bid, with the March 2027 review behind it [S16][S15]. The one regime date that could work the other way is 30 June 2027, when MSCI decides whether Indonesia stays in the emerging-market index or moves to Standalone status, after the consultation that closes for feedback on 30 April [S20]. Then come the full-year wholesale number, the FY2026 audited accounts with any refinancing disclosure, and the annual general meeting at which the parent dividend is declared [S6][S3][S8]. The volume test has largely passed — the ten-month market at 760,476 units has done the association's work — so the question is share and margin [S11][S13]. The audited accounts matter more: they show whether the nine-month operating outflow reversed and whether the short book was term-extended [S3].

We monitor quarterly operating cash flow and short-term loans, because those determine whether the funding structure holds; gross margin and the sales mix, the only lever the group controls; any related-party transaction, because at this float the controller can change the equity story without a market test; and any announcement touching the land and investment-property portfolio, because the withheld half of the reserve is the largest single lever on the target [S3][S5][S8].

We would revisit the rating on a corporate event, not a monthly sales beat: a disposal at appraised value, applied to debt reduction, would realise the withheld reserve and move equity value more than a year of volume growth [S5][S8]. Until then the shares trade below what the parts are worth, and the cushion is appraisal and book value rather than cash flow [S3][S5].

bear.narrative: A funding and governance discount, not a demand one: the group cannot roll 36,146.9bn of one-year financial liabilities at a 5% rate, a discounted equity raise to the controller dilutes minorities, and the admitted half of the appraisal reserve is at risk of never being realised. This case widens the discount only and does not revalue the block; the zero-admission end of the reserve range is run through the target in section 4. We keep the 30% weight despite a positive demand print because this case does not rest on the car market at all: October wholesales at +10% and the ten-month market at +19.7% [S13][S11] leave the funding and governance channel untouched. We widen the holdco discount to 55%, the tail of the house band [S3][S5].

bull.narrative: Two dated catalysts sit inside the twelve months and neither needs a car-market recovery: MSCI decides by end-June 2027 whether Indonesia stays in the emerging-market index or goes standalone [S20], and a placement of new shares to the public equal to about a tenth of the existing count at around Rp600 lifts the free float from 7.34% over the 15% floor, costs existing holders about 5% of NAV a share and restores index eligibility [S15]. Add a disposal or sale-and-leaseback at appraised value, which would realise the withheld half of the reserve, and the holdco discount compresses to 25% [S9][S8]. This is the mirror of the bear and is applied in the same amount; the reserve is not re-valued inside this case, only the discount on it.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-11-11): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S26]

index_deletions.note: 14 Indonesian HSC-category names deleted at the December 2026 review, effective at the open on 21 December 2026

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the reported nine months plus a fourth quarter grown at the latest monthly market rate: nine-month revenue of 27,492.6bn [S3] plus a fourth quarter at the 10.0% October market growth [S13][S14], which gives 18.2% for the full year rather than the 20% that the nine-month rate alone implied. The prior 20% required fourth-quarter revenue to accelerate to +17.1% on Q4-2025 against an October market at +10%, which no source supports; the market decelerated from the 21% nine-month rate to 19.7% at ten months [S6][S11]. From FY2027E growth fades toward the national market because Gaikindo wholesales reached 679,020 units in the nine months and 760,476 in the ten, against an 850,000 full-year target, while battery-electric entrants take share [S6][S7][S11][S13].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The nine months to September 2026 earned an 18.5% gross margin on 27,492.6bn of revenue, down from 20.1% in the same period a year earlier as vehicle discounting and a stronger yen cost of imported units bit [S3]. FY2026E carries that nine-month rate; the path back to the 20.4% audited FY2025A level by FY2030E assumes the spare-parts and workshop mix recovers as the fleet ages and the discounting cycle passes [S5][S10]. We do not hold a permanent margin haircut below the last audited year: the compression is cyclical and sourced, not structural.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the nine months to September 2026, which is clean of bargain-purchase gains: selling expenses of 1,591.0bn plus G&A of 1,646.3bn, less other operating income of 443.2bn and plus other operating expenses of 228.7bn, on revenue of 27,492.6bn is 11.0% [S3]. The FY2025 ratio of 11.1% is NOT used as the anchor because its 1,285.6bn of other operating income includes 413.9bn of one-off bargain-purchase gains (INA 389.165, RMM 2.053, ISJ 22.647) that do not recur [S5]. Carrying 11.0% therefore embeds no non-recurring income.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation and amortisation totalled 1,351.4bn on revenue of 30,505.5bn, or 4.4%, and the FY2024 total was 1,304.1bn; the Yahoo data pack carries only about a third of this, so the fact is restated from the note [S5]. We hold the ratio flat because the asset base is workshops and rental fleet, not a depreciating concession.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash capital expenditure was 2,890.2bn in FY2025 and 1,964.9bn in FY2024, or 9.5% and 6.7% of revenue; the FY2025 step-up funded the vehicle-rental fleet and the INA/Nissan assembly preparation [S5][S9]. FY2026E carries the FY2025 rate; the line then converges toward a steady state of D&A at 4.43% of revenue plus growth capex as the expansion spend rolls off, reaching 5.0% in the terminal year [S5]. Holding 8.5% in perpetuity grew the asset base twice as fast as revenue and was not a defensible long-run path.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital of 16,226.9bn against FY2025 revenue of 30,505.5bn is 53.2%, and we hold that level [S5]. It is NOT consumer-financing receivables alone: the multi-finance book is only 7,290.8bn net at December 2025 [S5]; the ratio is total trade and financing receivables, inventories and customer advances less payables, which is why 53.2% is the right description. FY2025A showed a 1,115.5bn working-capital release, but that was a one-year unwind of inventory and advances, not a new incremental ratio: holding the level at the last audited year is the anchor, and a growing finance book consumes cash with revenue growth.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set at the rate the LK actually pays, not the statutory 22%: income tax expense of 266,767m on pre-tax profit of 330,500m in the nine months to September 2026 is an 80.7% effective rate [S3 p.7], and FY2025A paid 61.8% [S5 note 18c]. The charge is quasi-fixed rather than proportional: it was almost unchanged year on year (266,767m against 266,083m) while pre-tax profit halved, because it carries non-deductible "Lain-lain", final-taxed dividend and rent income and deferred-tax movements that do not scale with profit [S3 p.7][S5 note 18c]. The engine taxes levered pre-tax profit, so the rate must reflect those permanent differences. We fade it toward the statutory rate as the loss-making assembly and distribution units return to profit and the non‑deductible base stops growing, with the terminal at the 22% statutory rate [S3][S5].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Finance charges of 2,033.8bn in the nine months to September 2026 annualise to 2,711.7bn against average gross debt near 54.5tn, a 5.0% rate, down from the 6.0% the three-year history implies as Bank Indonesia cut [S3][S5]. The group re-prices short-term working-capital loans quarterly, so the current rate, not the historical average, is the right forward input.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Finance income of 299.9bn in FY2025 against opening cash of 3,174.5bn is a 9.4% yield, but a large part is interest charged to related-party receivables rather than to deposits [S5][S3]. We use 5.5% on the deposit balance, close to the JIBOR-linked rate the treasury actually earns.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Gross debt rose from 51,288.0bn at December 2025 to 57,689.8bn at September 2026, with 15,266.6bn of short-term loans outstanding, because the operating cash outflow of 4,967.1bn was funded with borrowings [S3]. Nine months of 2026 already added 6,401.8bn of gross debt and pushed net debt to 54,531.2bn, so FY2026E must carry at least that and a fourth quarter funded the same way: we set 12,000bn, which funds the nine-month outflow and a similar fourth quarter rather than assuming the gap closes [S3]. The engine builds cash as the balancing item, so the forecast net-debt line is still driven by FCFF and remains below the September actual; section 3 discloses the gap and the scenario build does not depend on it. The line then declines as revenue growth slows: 8,000, 5,000, 3,000 and 2,000bn.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 equity in net earnings of associates was 73.3bn and final income tax was 34.4bn, both reported below the operating line, leaving 38.9bn of net other items [S5]. We hold that run-rate flat rather than extrapolating the 211.3bn of associate earnings booked in FY2024, which included one-off gains at the joint ventures.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests took 100.1bn of the 232.4bn FY2025 net profit, or 43.1%, because the profitable multi-finance and rental subsidiaries carry large outside stakes while the wholly-owned distribution arm lost money [S5][S3]. The three-year average of 32% understates the current share, so we use 42%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was 15.98bn, or Rp4 a share, a 12.1% payout of the 132.3bn parent profit, while minorities took a further 145.7bn [S5][S8]. With a 4,967.1bn operating cash outflow in the nine months to September 2026, 36,146.9bn of financial liabilities maturing within a year and only 3,158.6bn of cash, we assume the parent dividend is suspended through the forecast rather than funded with new debt [S3].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Issued shares have been 3,994,291,039 since the 2019 rights issue and no new mandate is disclosed in the FY2025 accounts [S5]. A discounted placement to the controlling shareholder is carried as a bear-case dilution risk in §5, not in the base share count, because no share issuance has been announced [S5][S8].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Terminal growth of 4% is below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP and below the 5% the house card allows for a compounder; it is retained for the FCFF cross-check arithmetic even though the target is built on the parts, because the SOTP carries the asset marks and the DCF only frames the cash throw [S5].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Held at 40%, the wide end of the 20-40% house band, and argued rather than asserted. The governance file justifies the wide end: Gallant Venture holds 49.49% and the free float is 7.34%, related-party purchases are 4,902.6bn or 22% of cost of revenue, and other receivables from related parties are 3,220.2bn [S8][S3]. The name own history supports the wide end rather than the midpoint: its reported P/B has run 0.27x (FY2024A), 0.42x (FY2023A), 0.29x (FY2022A) and 0.34x (FY2025A), and the 52-week range of the price (high and low in the data pack) brackets 0.40x to 0.21x of book, so the market has never paid anything close to the parts and there is no 5-year episode of a narrow discount to point to [S0]. The house base rate for discount narrowing (data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing) completes only 33% of the time over three years with a +28%/-18% spread, so the discount is not assumed to narrow; it is the base rate and governance is its DNA. The scenario tails run to 55% (bear) and 25% (bull) because the discount is the only channel the scenario layer has into a balance-sheet mark.

challenges.challenge: The HOLD rests on 'the tape does not support it, the shares having traded up to Rp695 through the announcement [S0][S16]'. The price is the 13 November close (datapack price_date 2026-11-13) and S16 was published 14 November 15:15 WIB, so no price in the file can reflect that announcement. Rp695 is also 3% above the 52-week low of Rp675 and 50% below the Rp1,385 high, and the prior draft called the same level the floor of the range.
challenges.answer: Deleted the tape claim. The 13 November close of Rp695 predates the 14 November 15:15 WIB FTSE announcement, so no trade in the file can reflect it; the report now says exactly that and places the price near the 52-week low of Rp675, 50% below the high, instead of reading it as resilience [S0][S16].

challenges.challenge: The entire Rp6,928.5bn appraisal surplus is set to zero (non-IMJ block Rp1,839.0bn at cost), yet s4 concedes the marks are genuine independent market-approach appraisals. One stated reason is that 'the shares have never traded near appraised book' - that bends a fundamental input to the share price, which VAL_KONGLO_REGIME s1 forbids. Rp1,735 a share pre-discount, Rp1,010 in twelve-month value, 2.2x the whole of the current fundamental.
challenges.answer: Admitted half the Rp6,928.5bn appraisal reserve (Rp3,464.3bn) in the non-IMJ block on asset reasons only: the marks are independent appraisals and no sale or sale-and-leaseback is disclosed. The price-bent reason is gone. Base fundamental is now Rp887 and the price 0.88x it; zero admission gives a HOLD at Rp646, full admission a BUY at Rp898, all three run through the target in section 4 [S3][S5].

challenges.challenge: The twelve-month roll uses a 21.2% cost of equity - 7.45% rf, 2.30 levered beta at 2.00 gearing - outside the 11-13% house COE band and justified in one sentence as used only to roll a balance-sheet mark. The roll adds Rp80.7 to the fundamental (Rp380.5 to Rp461.3); at a 12% roll the weighted target is about Rp646, i.e. Rp53 or 7.6% of the price, taking expected return from +0.6% to -7.1%.
challenges.answer: The roll now uses a band-consistent 11.9% cost of equity: the -9.3pp company adjustment removes the leverage premium the engine adds by levering the asset beta at the capped 2.0x consolidated gearing, which the SOTP already prices once through the holdco discount. The report discloses the Rp792.4 unrolled value as the denominator of the 0.88x ratio, and the target is Rp803 at that rate [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: The prior call was SELL with a target of Rp461 at a price of Rp680; the same fundamental, undistinguished, now yields Rp699 and HOLD because the konglo lens applies 1.515x. The report says the rating is now HOLD but never states the prior rating, the prior target, or that the lens - triggered by the 11 November HSC listing rather than the 14 November FTSE news - is the entire change.
challenges.answer: The Investment summary now states that the prior published call was a sell with a target below the price, and attributes the change to the 11 November HSC listing that triggers the lens plus this revision admission of half the reserve. It says plainly that neither the FTSE deletion nor the assets moved the call [S16][S19].

challenges.challenge: MSCI opened a consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone on 15 October 2026, feedback to 30 April 2027, decision by 30 June 2027 - inside the twelve-month window and the remaining index event after the FTSE deletion. It is the regime catalyst the konglo deck names, yet the report omits it from s5, s7 and the frontmatter and uses 30 June 2027 only for the AGM.
challenges.answer: MSCI added with dates: consultation opened 15 October 2026, feedback to 30 April 2027, decision by end-June 2027 [S20]; it is now a frontmatter catalyst, a section 5 paragraph stating that an adverse decision pushes the closure share from the base 25% toward the bear -20%, and a section 7 signpost.

challenges.challenge: Neither the 13 November IHSG exit nor the 21 December FTSE deletion is sized. ADTV is Rp250m a day against a Rp2.78tn market cap; the report asserts a forced seller the float cannot absorb with no number, and the base 35% compression is not tied to any flow.
challenges.answer: The flows are sized: ADTV is Rp250.4m against a Rp2.78tn market capitalisation and a 7.34% float, so the whole free float is several years of average daily turnover and any tracker exit needs a price concession. The base 25% and bear -20% closure shares are now tied to that bound rather than asserted [S0][S17].

challenges.challenge: The operating franchise is carried at negative net assets (investments of Rp4,300.4bn alone exceed the Rp1,839.0bn block) and no value is attached to Rp24,293.5bn of distribution revenue, the Suzuki franchise or the INA assembly acquisition. No scenario contains an operating shock, so the upside from the business the group actually runs is never tested.
challenges.answer: The block already carries the operating subsidiaries at book; the negative residual is the parent corporate debt, and the automotive segment lost Rp4,075.9bn at the net level in FY2025 [S5]. Putting a revenue-based value on a franchise that loses money would capitalise the losses, so we floor it at zero and test recovery through the operating catalysts and the discount, not through a revenue multiple [S3][S5].

challenges.challenge: A discounted placement or rights issue appears only as a bear item, a downside not a remedy. The same transaction closes the 7.66pp free-float gap and is the one documented route back over the 15% floor and into the indices; the report never runs it as an upside, and it is the mirror of a bear it does run.
challenges.answer: The placement is now run both ways: as the bear dilution and as the one documented route out of the regime. Issuing roughly a tenth of the share count at a discount closes the 7.66pp float gap over the 15% floor, costs existing holders a few per cent of NAV a share and restores index eligibility; we give it a one-in-four probability inside the window [S15][S17].

challenges.challenge: The 91.97% IMJS block, Rp1,367.0bn or 43% of the SOTP, is marked at market. IMJS is covered (own report, fundamental Rp137.69) and is itself on the HSC list at 94.879% with an 8.03% float and out of the IHSG since 13 November (S19). VAL_KONGLO_REGIME s4 requires a covered sibling at house fundamental, pre-lens; the value difference is only about Rp6.9bn, but the report never discloses that its largest block is priced by a market in the same regime.
challenges.answer: The IMJS block is re-marked at the subsidiary house fundamental of Rp137.69, pre-lens, giving Rp1,373.8bn against Rp1,367.0bn at market, a Rp6.8bn difference. Sections 4 and 6 now label it, and disclose IMJS 94.879% HSC concentration, its 8.03% float and its IHSG exit on 13 November [S19][S5].

challenges.challenge: The ladder is misdescribed: 'Undiscounted that book is worth Rp482 a share; after the discount and the liquidity ladder it is Rp461'. Rp482 is already after the 40% holdco discount - the undiscounted NAV is Rp802.6 - and the ladder takes Rp481.6 to Rp385.3; Rp461 is the probability-weighted twelve-month value after the roll. The sentence implies a 4% cut where the stack removes 52%.
challenges.answer: Ladder restated in the order the engine applies it, all as placeholders: Rp1,003 after the 40% holdco discount, Rp1,109 after the twelve-month roll and the 45/30/25 business weights, Rp887 after the 20% ladder, then the lens to Rp803. The sentence no longer implies a small cut and now names the holdco discount as the large step [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: The regime weights (base 50, bear 25, bull 25) are never stated, so Rp699 cannot be reproduced from Rp682, Rp536 and Rp895. The 25% bull assumes the premium re-expands 10% of the log gap after the last index bid leaves on 21 December, with the float deadline in 2029 and no controller action pending; no catalyst is named. Re-weighting bear to 50% and base to 25% gives Rp662, a negative expected return.
challenges.answer: Regime weights are stated (50% base, 25% bear, 25% bull) and the bull now has named dated catalysts: an MSCI retention decision by 30 June 2027, a float-fixing placement and a disposal at appraised value [S20]. Doubling the bear weight gives Rp792, still +13.9% and an ADD, so the call does not rest on the weight.

challenges.challenge: Three citations do not carry the claim: the one-in-three NAV-discount narrowing is the house base rate (data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing), not [S0]; the 7.4% risk-free rate is cited to [S0][S5], neither of which contains a risk-free rate; and ten holder names [S19] is not in S19, which gives only the 95.484% figure.
challenges.answer: Re-cited: the risk-free rate to the ten-year SBN yield of 7.65% on 10 November 2026 [S21], the one-in-three discount-narrowing base rate to the internal base-rate file by name rather than [S0], and the ten-holder framing dropped for the 95.484% HSC figure the source actually carries [S19].

challenges.challenge: The IMJS basis text states the mark is Rp135 and 10,849.3m shares (market capitalisation 1,464.7bn), but the modelled value of Rp1,367.0bn equals 1,486.3bn x 91.97%, i.e. the Rp137 datapack price, and the IMJS mark date (11 November) differs from the parent price date (13 November) inside one valuation.
challenges.answer: The IMJS basis text now carries the figures the engine uses: Rp137.69 fundamental x 10,849.3m shares x 91.97% = Rp1,373.8bn, and it notes the market alternative it replaced was Rp137 a share and Rp1,486.3bn capitalisation, not Rp135 and Rp1,464.7bn. Mark dates are aligned to the 13 November close [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: No operating bull anywhere: the distribution/assembly franchise (Rp24,293.5bn revenue, Suzuki 7.8% share) is carried at negative net book, and the only business shock is holdco_discount +/-15pp, so no scenario tests an operating recovery. A float-fixing placement appears only as dilution, never as the one sourced route back over the 15% floor.

missing_bear_case.note: The MSCI Standalone consultation (opened 15 Oct 2026, decision by 30 Jun 2027) is absent from s5, s7 and the frontmatter, though it falls inside the window and the report itself uses that date for the AGM. The FTSE and IHSG outflows are never sized against ADTV of Rp250m a day.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are the discount stack, the appraisal treatment and the cost-of-capital roll. The 40% holdco discount is argued and unchanged by this update (credit), but a 20% liquidity ladder sits on top of it and the 21.2% COE roll is outside the house band; no driver moves operating value at all.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified: F48/F49/F51/F52 wholesales bases reconcile exactly (561,405 + 74,051 = 635,456); F20 dividend split 15.977 vs 145.733; F8 D&A; F70 HSC 95.484%; S16 names IMAS among the 14; S3 tax 266,767 vs 266,083. Wrong: the tape claim, the 482 label and three mis-citations.

valuation_method_fit.note: SOTP is the right method for a holdco and the 100% weight is properly argued. Two faults: the IMJS block is marked at market though IMJS is covered and itself HSC, which VAL_KONGLO_REGIME s4 forbids, and a 21.2% COE outside the 11-13% house band rolls a balance-sheet mark forward twelve months.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose reads more than the evidence at exactly the two points that decide the call: the tape is described as holding through news that postdates the price, and the regime bull (premium re-expands, Rp895) is asserted with no named catalyst. Doubling the regime bear weight gives Rp662, a negative expected return.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity or royalty variable binds this name; the model reads volume, ASP and margin rather than benchmark or royalty, consistent with the autos peers. The one gap is that the macro deck usd_idr path is unused while s5 calls the rupiah a live cost and debt risk.

conservatism_audit.note: Justified: terminal capex 5.0%, zero payout, revenue Q4 at the October market rate, tax at the LK 80.7%, gross margin at the 9M rate. Unjustified: the whole Rp6,928.5bn appraisal surplus at zero, and the wide-end discount plus a 20% ladder stacked. Shocks are exactly mirrored, so no asymmetry there.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin 11.9% against FY2025A 13.7% is the -1.75pp gap and it is sourced to the 9M gross margin of 18.5% in s3. Both BLOCK flags are justified by sources that say what is claimed (F20, F8). FY2026E parent profit 56.1 against an annualised 9M 20.2 is disclosed in s3 and does not feed the target.

signoff.notes: Signed ADD, target Rp803, price Rp695, TR +15.6% (band +10 to +25), on a 12-month fundamental of Rp887 and a konglo lens that keeps 0.906 of it; the 50/25/25 regime weights reproduce Rp803. Both FATALs are answered on substance: the 13 Nov close is no longer described as trading through the 14 Nov FTSE news, and the Rp6.93tn appraisal reserve is half-admitted on asset grounds with the price-bent reason removed; the reserve ties to the LK (3,607.1 land + 3,240.0 investment property = 6,847.1 at FY2025; +81.4 land movement = 6,928.5 at 9M2026) and the 1,003 -> 1,109 -> 887 -> 803 ladder reproduces in the engine. On the QC FIX/NOTE items I agree none undermines the call, with one correction to QC. Q1 (0.88 paired with 887) is a real text error but conservative: the correct discount to the 12-month value is 0.78 and the direction is unchanged. Q2 is wrong and should not be applied: re-running the engine lens, zero reserve admission makes the price a premium (695/381 = 1.82, kept 1.51x) and gives target Rp646, TR -7.1%, HOLD; full admission gives Rp898, +29.3%, BUY - exactly the analyst's s4 paragraph and C2 response; QC's Rp386/-44% and Rp1,220/+76% apply the discount-direction factor to a premium case. Q3 units, Q4 direction wording (HSC cuts 5pp from the closing share in a discount; the 25% base is right), Q5 rf citation (7.45% vs S21 7.65%, COE about 12.1% still in band), Q6 bull citations and Q7-Q10 are presentation or citation and do not move the rating. Residuals for the next version, none blocking: section 5 says the base leaves 25% of the gap unclosed where section 4 correctly says it closes 25% (should be leaves 75%); the prior published target (Rp458) is not printed, the summary says only a target below the price; the IMJS mark is the sibling 12-month fundamental (Rp137.69) used as a today mark in a NAV that is then rolled another 12 months (about Rp14 a share, under 2%, disclosed); and the report does not engage the house macro regime (consumer-discretionary AVOID, usd_idr path unused), though this is an asset-value call. Bias check: single name at signoff, but note IMAS is the only AUTOS_COMPONENTS name with WACC below 11% at 8.9%; it does not enter the SOTP because no cash flow is discounted, so not a defect. The flip from the 10 Nov SELL is honestly attributed to the 11 Nov HSC listing plus correction of the prior reserve zeroing, not to the 14 Nov FTSE news.

bias.note: Base 45% >= 40%; the business bear and bull shock the SAME driver by mirrored +/-15pp holdco discount, and the bear's extra 5pp weight is sourced to the funding/governance channel that the positive October volume print does not touch [S13][S3]. Every departure from the FY2025A actual is sourced or argued: FY2026E gross margin 18.5% is the reported 9M2026 actual (20.1% prior year) [S3]; tax 80.7% is the LK's effective charge and fades to statutory [S3][S5]; capex 9.47%->5.0% is answered with the FY2024 6.7% / FY2025 9.5% history [S5]. The COE adjustment (21.2% -> 11.9%) LOWERS the target, so inputs are not bent toward the price, and the reserve is half-admitted on asset reasons, not on the quote. No unsourced default haircut found. Residual: FY2027E revenue growth 10% and FY2028E 8% are typed without a source in params_basis, but they do not enter the SOTP target (FCFF cross-check only) - NOTE Q8.

recomputed.item: Net debt at 30-Sep-2026 (debt 57,734.6 incl. lease liabilities less cash 3,163.6)
SOTP NAV (IMJS 1,373.8 + non-IMJ 5,303.2; parent equity 13,786.5 less IMJ attributable book 5,019.0 less withheld half-reserve 3,464.3)

findings.finding: Investment summary pairs {{val.konglo.premium_ratio}} (0.88) with {{val.tp_fundamental}} (887): 'The parts are worth Rp887 a share against Rp695, so the shares trade at 0.88 times what the assets justify'. The engine premium_ratio is price over fundamental value TODAY (695 / 792.4 = 0.877), not over the 12-month value; 695 / 887 = 0.78. Section 4 states the mechanics correctly.

Section 4 appraisal-range paragraph is typed, not engine, and both ends are wrong: zero admission gives NAV 3,212.7bn, Rp804 a share, a target near Rp386 and an expected return near -44%, a SELL on the -25% sell band - not 'a hold with a negative expected return', which also contradicts section 1 and review record C4 (prior call was a SELL at Rp461). Full admission gives about Rp1,220 and +76%, not 'a quarter above the price'. The paragraph conclusion (a sell needs a move to one extreme) is right; its middle numbers are not.

Section 5 prints the flows with the data in rupiah and a bn suffix attached: 'Average daily turnover is IDR250,423,269.8bn against a market capitalisation of IDR2,776,032,272,105.0bn'. Engine market: adtv_idr = Rp250,423,269.84 (Rp0.25bn) and mcap = IDR2,776.0bn (Rp2.78tn). Both are 1,000x too large, in the paragraph the red team asked to be sized (C6). The several-years-of-turnover arithmetic behind them is right at 3.3 years.

Section 4 says 'HSC membership adds 5% to the closing share'. For a discount the deck SUBTRACTS the HSC adjustment: compress base 0.30 - 0.05 = 0.25, which is why the base closes 25% not 30% (model val.konglo.compress.base 0.25 with adj_hsc +0.05).

Section 4 cites 'the 7.4% risk-free rate the house deck takes from the ten-year government yield [S21]'. S21 (10 November 2026) reports the 10-year at 7.65% (13-year 7.75%); the model uses rf 7.45%. The citation does not carry the number, and this input was the subject of C12.

The bull scenario narrative cites [S9][S8] for 'a disposal or sale-and-leaseback at appraised value'. S9 is the 99.9% INA/NMI acquisition report and S8 the June 2026 dividend article; neither discloses a disposal or sale-and-leaseback. The disclosure is that none is disclosed, as section 4 says.

Konglo registry has groups: [] for IMAS while section 6 names the Salim group and Gallant Venture at 49.49% [S8]. Profile facts check out: HSC 95.484% [S19], the FTSE deletion of 21 December including IMAS among the nine micro caps [S16], free float 7.34% vs the 15% floor with the next step 31 March 2029, and no enforcement.

FY2027E revenue growth 10% and FY2028E 8% are typed without a source in params_basis. They do not reach the target (SOTP; the FCFF cross-check floors at zero), but the method card asks for a sourced reason on every drift from the last actual (FY2025A 4.0%).

Report is 4,991 words against the 500-3,500 update band (analyst disclosed 4,519). Section 7 also says the 21 December deletion leaves 'the March 2027 review behind it' when that review is ahead of us.

The packet generic bridge prints net debt 54,570.9, minorities 2,552.2 and associates 2,580.6 while the SOTP applies holdco_net_debt 0.0 by design (the parts are equity values already net of subsidiary debt and NCI). The audit confirms nothing is double-counted, but the display invites the reader to think consolidated net debt is deducted from a NAV that already carries it.

flags.justification: SOTP is weighted at 100% because it is the only method that produces a value for a holding company whose listed stake trades at 0.27x book and whose consolidated FCFF is negative [S5][S3]; P/E on true LTM parent earnings of -110.1bn is unavailable and EV/EBITDA floors at zero, so weighting them would put 70% of the blend on methods that return zero, which the red team correctly rejected.
